definition: The CLEVER (Cross Lipschitz Extreme Value for nEtwork Robustness) score is a way of measuring the robustness of an artificial neural network towards adversarial attacks.
details: It was developed by a team at the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab in IBM Research and first presented at the 2018 International Conference on Learning Representations. It was mentioned and reviewed by Ian Goodfellow as well. It was adopted into an educational game Fool The Bank by Narendra Nath Joshi, Abhishek Bhandwaldar and Casey Dugan

explainer.lead: The CLEVER score estimates how robust an artificial neural network is to adversarial attacks. It gives researchers a way to assess resistance to manipulated inputs instead of judging a model only by its ordinary accuracy.

tiers.eli5: Imagine checking how easily a tower of blocks falls when someone gives it small, sneaky pushes. CLEVER does something similar for an AI system: it estimates how well the system holds up when inputs are deliberately changed to confuse it.
tiers.practitioner: Use CLEVER as a robustness metric when evaluating neural networks against adversarial attacks, alongside ordinary task-performance metrics. A higher score indicates greater estimated robustness, but it is not proof that no attack can succeed. Take care when comparing results produced under different evaluation settings.
tiers.paperLevel: CLEVER (Cross Lipschitz Extreme Value for nEtwork Robustness) is a score for estimating the adversarial robustness of an artificial neural network. It was developed by a team at the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab in IBM Research and first presented at the 2018 International Conference on Learning Representations. The score concerns estimated robustness, not a guarantee of security against every attack.

explainer.example: A team evaluates an image classifier with CLEVER, then repeats the evaluation after changing the model to improve its attack resistance. If the second evaluation produces a higher CLEVER score, the revised model is estimated to be more robust, while its ordinary classification accuracy still needs to be checked separately.

explainer.measures: CLEVER measures an artificial neural network's estimated robustness to adversarial attacks, rather than its accuracy on ordinary inputs.
howScored: CLEVER expresses the network's estimated adversarial robustness as a score, with a higher result indicating greater robustness. It is not a percentage of correct predictions or a guarantee that the network is attack-proof.
caveats: A CLEVER score is not a guarantee against every adversarial attack.
Robustness evaluation does not replace ordinary accuracy or task-performance testing.
Do not assume scores from different evaluation settings are directly comparable.
